Rom90 - One-way functions are necessary and sufficient for secure signatures
sources.note: STOC 1990, pp. 387-394. Context on this page: EUF-CMA signatures follow from OWFs alone, without iO.

pages.class_justification: The construction obfuscates circuits that hardwire the code of the puncturable PRF/PRG derived from the one-way function, so it is non-black-box in the OWF hypothesis (punctured programming is the standard example of a non-black-box use of a primitive; the Asharov-Segev FOCS 2015 framework exists precisely because such constructions fall outside the black-box taxonomy). iO itself is invoked only as an algorithm on circuits. No finer RTV04 placement is stated in the literature, so per the schema convention an explicitly non-black-box construction is recorded as free.
pages.statement: [[indistinguishability-obfuscation|Indistinguishability obfuscation]] for all polynomial-size circuits together with a [[hash-function|one-way function]] implies [[digital-signature|digital signatures]]: the Sahai-Waters punctured-programming construction is hash-and-sign, has short signatures with fast verification, and is proved selectively secure — [[SW14 - How to Use Indistinguishability Obfuscation Deniable Encryption, and More|SW14]].
pages.sketch: The signing key is a puncturable PRF key $K$; the signature on $m$ is $\sigma = F(K, m)$, and the verification key is an obfuscated program that accepts $(m, \sigma)$ iff $f(\sigma) = f(F(K, m))$ for a one-way function $f$. Puncturing $K$ at the target message and replacing $F(K, m^*)$ by a uniform value reduces forgery to inverting $f$.
pages.improvements_text: - Adaptively secure EUF-CMA signatures follow from one-way functions alone, without iO — [[Rom90 - One-way functions are necessary and sufficient for secure signatures|Rom90]]; the iO construction's point is short signatures with fast verification.
flags: SW14 proves selective security; the ds page's default notion is adaptive EUF-CMA. The statement preserves the qualifier.
Edge is redundant as an existence claim: OWF alone implies EUF-CMA signatures (Rom90, see hash-function-to-ds); the SW14 edge is only interesting for the short/fast-verification qualifier.

sources.ref_file_title: KK05 - On Constructing Universal One-Way Hash Functions from Arbitrary One-Way Functions
sources.note: First complete write-up of Rompel's proof; documents gaps in the STOC version.

pages.class_justification: The construction uses the one-way function only as an oracle (the UOWHF, the one-time signatures, and the authentication tree are all built by evaluating $f$), and the security reduction runs any forger as an oracle to either find a UOWHF collision or invert $f$. The NY89/Rom90 route is routinely treated in the black-box-separations literature as the canonical fully black-box construction of signatures from OWFs.
pages.statement: If [[hash-function|one-way functions]] exist, then EUF-CMA-secure [[digital-signature|digital signatures]] exist — [[Rom90 - One-way functions are necessary and sufficient for secure signatures|Rom90]]. The construction builds universal one-way hash functions from any one-way function and instantiates the tree-based signature paradigm of [[NY89 - Universal one-way hash functions and their cryptographic applications|NY89]].
pages.sketch: Rompel constructs universal one-way hash functions from any one-way function; UOWHFs compress messages for one-time signatures, and authenticating a tree of fresh one-time keys (Naor-Yung) yields many-time EUF-CMA signatures.
pages.improvements_text:
- Signatures from one-way *permutations*, via universal one-way hash functions and the tree-based paradigm Rompel instantiates — [[NY89 - Universal one-way hash functions and their cryptographic applications|NY89]].
- Rompel's STOC version contains gaps; the first complete write-up of the proof is [[KK05 - On Constructing Universal One-Way Hash Functions from Arbitrary One-Way Functions|KK05]].
flags: kind left as implication: the converse direction exists as its own page (ds-to-hash-function), so the OWF <=> DS equivalence is split across two pages per the schema convention.

The second migrated quote (post-quantum hash-based signatures from collision resistance) belongs to the hash-based-signature edges (hash-function-to-hash-based-signatures-lam79 / hash-based-signatures-to-ds-mer89), not this edge; the digital-signature page also states that hypothesis two incompatible ways (collision resistance vs second-preimage resistance + pseudorandomness) — prose fix needed there.

sources.ref_file_title: SW14 - How to Use Indistinguishability Obfuscation Deniable Encryption, and More
sources.note: Supplies the PKE and (statistically simulation-sound) NIZK components from iO + OWF via punctured programming; [GGHRSW13, SW14] is the standard joint citation for FE from iO + OWF.

pages.class_justification: The construction obfuscates circuits that hardwire the code of the puncturable PRF/PRG derived from the one-way function, so it is non-black-box in the OWF hypothesis (punctured programming is the standard example of a non-black-box use of a primitive; the Asharov-Segev FOCS 2015 framework exists precisely because such constructions fall outside the black-box taxonomy). iO itself is invoked only as an algorithm on circuits. No finer RTV04 placement is stated in the literature, so per the schema convention an explicitly non-black-box construction is recorded as free.
pages.statement: [[indistinguishability-obfuscation|iO]] for all polynomial-size circuits together with a [[hash-function|one-way function]] implies indistinguishability-secure [[functional-encryption|functional encryption]] for all polynomial-size circuits: [[GGHRSW13 - Candidate indistinguishability obfuscation and functional encryption for all circuits|GGHRSW13]] build FE from iO, [[public-key-encryption|PKE]], and statistically simulation-sound [[non-interactive-zero-knowledge|NIZK]], and the latter two follow from iO plus one-way functions — [[SW14 - How to Use Indistinguishability Obfuscation Deniable Encryption, and More|SW14]].
pages.sketch: A ciphertext encrypts $m$ under two PKE keys together with a statistically simulation-sound NIZK that both components encrypt the same message; the functional key for $f$ is an obfuscation of the program that verifies the proof, decrypts one component, and outputs $f(m)$. Security is a Naor-Yung-style hybrid, using iO to switch which key the functional key decrypts.
flags: GGHRSW13 as published assumes iO + injective one-way functions + PKE + statistically simulation-sound NIZK; the {iO, OWF} form quoted in the wiki is the standard joint citation [GGHRSW13, SW14] after instantiating the components via punctured programming — verified against the GGHRSW13 abstract.
GGHRSW13's FE is selectively secure; adaptive security came later (e.g. Waters, CRYPTO 2015 — not added as a source).
Conclusion slug functional-encryption still has no wiki page (migration note remains true).

pages.wrong_reason: SW14 does not construct lossy (trapdoor) functions. Its result list (verified against the abstract) is: deniable encryption, PKE, short selectively secure hash-and-sign signatures, CCA-secure PKE, NIZKs, *injective* trapdoor functions, and oblivious transfer; the migrated bullet's 'lossy functions' appears to be a garbling of 'injective trapdoor functions'. Moreover the edge {OWF, iO} => lossy trapdoor functions is not merely unattributed but untenable as stated: sufficiently lossy functions imply collision-resistant hashing (Peikert-Waters, STOC 2008, fully black-box), and Asharov-Segev (FOCS 2015, eprint 2015/341) rule out constructions of CRHFs from iO + OWFs even in a model capturing SW14-style non-black-box punctured-programming constructions; no such construction is known. The defensible corrected edge is {hash-function, io} => injective trapdoor functions — SW14.
flags: HIGH PRIORITY: re-point this page to injective trapdoor functions (SW14) or delete it; also fix the source bullet on indistinguishability-obfuscation § Other results ('iO + OWF -> deniable encryption, lossy functions, ...').
SW14 full text could not be fetched in this environment (eprint/ACM egress blocked); the result list was verified from the abstract via web search, which does not mention lossy functions.

sources.ref_file_title: GGM86 - How to construct random functions
sources.authors: Oded Goldreich, Shafi Goldwasser, Silvio Micali
sources.note: Sources the PRG => PRF link of the composite chain.

pages.class_justification: Each link is fully black-box — HILL99's PRG from any OWF, the GGM tree PRF, and PRF-as-MAC all invoke the hypothesis only as an oracle and run the adversary only as an oracle — and fully-black-box reductions compose (RTV04).
pages.statement: If [[hash-function|one-way functions]] exist, then UF-CMA [[message-authentication-code|MACs]] exist: any one-way function yields a [[pseudorandom-generator|PRG]] [[HILL99 - A Pseudorandom Generator from Any One-Way Function|HILL99]], any length-doubling PRG yields a [[pseudorandom-function|PRF]] [[GGM86 - How to construct random functions|GGM86]], and setting $\Tag(k, m) := \Eval(k, m)$ with canonical verification gives a UF-CMA MAC — the last step is folklore.
pages.sketch: A forger that outputs a valid tag on an unqueried message predicts the PRF value $\Eval(k, \hat{m})$, which a truly random function permits only with probability $1/|\calT|$; any successful forger therefore yields a PRF distinguisher.
flags: Composite chain OWF => PRG => PRF => MAC; every link exists as its own page (hash-function-to-prg-hill99, prg-to-prf-ggm86, prf-to-mac). Repo policy splits composite chains — a human should decide whether to keep this corollary edge or delete it in favor of the links.
The second migrated quote (CCA-secure SKE via encrypt-then-MAC, Bellare-Namprempre) belongs to mac-and-ske-to-cca-security, not this edge.
The composite security loss is dominated by the large polynomial loss of the HILL99 OWF => PRG step; not stated crisply enough anywhere to fill security_loss.

sources.ref_file_title: Lam79 - Constructing digital signatures from a one way function

sources.note: Winternitz variant (and Merkle trees, which belong to the separate mer89 edge).

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction that evaluates the one-way function only as an oracle (key generation hashes random preimages; verification re-hashes revealed preimages), and one fixed reduction that runs any forger once as an oracle, planting its inversion challenge at a random key position and answering the single signing query with the remaining preimages. The RTV04 fully-black-box shape.
pages.statement: A [[hash-function|one-way function]] implies one-time [[digital-signature#hash-based-signatures|digital signatures]] (Lamport's scheme): for $\ell$-bit messages, the signing key is $2\ell$ random preimages $x_{i,b}$, the verification key is their images $y_{i,b} = \hash(k, x_{i,b})$, and the signature on $m$ reveals $(x_{i,m_i})_{i \le \ell}$; each key pair may sign only one message — [[Lam79 - Constructing digital signatures from a one way function|Lam79]].
pages.sketch: A forger on a fresh message $\hat{m} \ne m$ must reveal a preimage of some unopened $y_{i, 1-m_i}$; the reduction plants its one-wayness challenge at a random one of the $2\ell$ positions, answers the single signing query with the remaining preimages, and inverts $\hash(k, \cdot)$ whenever the forgery opens the planted slot — a $2\ell$ loss.
pages.improvements_text: - The Winternitz variant signs several message bits per hash chain, trading signature size for $\hash$ evaluations; it first appears in print in [[Mer89 - A Certified Digital Signature|Mer89]].
notes_to_keep: SUSPECTED ERROR (reported, not fixed): the digital-signature page's 'sign one bit per hash chain' describes WINTERNITZ, not Lamport. Lamport publishes two hash images per message bit and reveals one preimage per bit; there are no chains.
SUSPECTED EFFICIENCY ERROR: Lamport signatures are $O(\secpar \cdot |m|)$ bits for an $|m|$-bit message (typically $O(\secpar^2)$ with hashed messages), not $O(\secpar)$.
flags: One-wayness (preimage resistance) of the hash suffices; the CRHF/OWF conflation on the hash-function page makes the hypothesis look stronger than needed.

The Merkle-tree many-time extension is the separate edge hash-based-signatures-to-ds-mer89; the OWF-only route there needs UOWHFs (NY89/Rom90) for the tree, a caveat recorded on those pages' source text.
Pseudocode contains three algorithm environments (KeyGen, Sign, Vrfy); the editor may need to fence them separately.

sources.ref_file_title: KPV22 - RedShift Transparent SNARKs from List Polynomial Commitments
sources.authors: Assimakis A. Kattis, Konstantin Panarin, Alexander Vlasov
sources.note: Makes the FRI-based (list) polynomial commitment abstraction explicit. Verified: CCS 2022, doi 10.1145/3548606.3560657.

pages.class_justification: The commitment uses the hash only as an oracle (Merkle trees over codeword evaluations), but the compiled non-interactive scheme is proven secure with the hash modeled as a random oracle rather than against a standard-model CRHF adversary, and no RTV04 placement for the compiled argument appears in the literature; recording a class would add a claim.
pages.model_justification: FRI is an IOP of proximity; the commitment scheme Merkle-hashes the prover's oracles and is made non-interactive by the BCS/Fiat-Shamir compilation, whose soundness is proven with the hash modeled as a random oracle (this is the model of BBHR18's non-interactive STARK). Interactively, binding rests on collision resistance alone. Frontmatter should change standard -> rom; the page's own migration note already flags this.
pages.statement: [[hash-function|Collision-resistant hash functions]] yield a transparent [[polynomial-commitment|polynomial commitment scheme]]: commit to a polynomial of degree $< d$ by Merkle-hashing its Reed-Solomon codeword, and prove low-degreeness and openings with the FRI proximity test, giving $O(\log^2 d)$-size proofs and verification with no trusted setup; the non-interactive scheme is proven secure in the random-oracle model — [[BBHR18 - Scalable, transparent, and post-quantum secure computational integrity|BBHR18]].
pages.sketch: FRI repeatedly folds the committed codeword: writing $f_i(x) = g_i(x^2) + x\,h_i(x^2)$, the verifier sends a random $\alpha_i$ and the prover commits to the codeword of $f_{i+1}(y) = g_i(y) + \alpha_i h_i(y)$, halving the degree each round; consistency is spot-checked at random points via Merkle openings.
pages.improvements_text: - The polynomial-commitment abstraction of FRI (as a *list* polynomial commitment) is made explicit and used to build transparent SNARKs — [[KPV22 - RedShift Transparent SNARKs from List Polynomial Commitments|KPV22]].
flags: BBHR18 introduces FRI and STARKs but does not itself define a polynomial commitment scheme; the PCS framing is a later, now-standard abstraction (made explicit in RedShift, KPV22). The slug's -bbhr18 attribution is kept per the slug rule, with this caveat.

Opening at an arbitrary evaluation point $z$ uses the standard quotient trick (proximity of $(f(x)-f(z))/(x-z)$), made explicit in later works (DEEP-FRI, RedShift); BBHR18 itself uses FRI as a low-degree test inside STARKs.
Frontmatter model must change standard -> rom.
Strictly, FRI commitments bind to a low-degree *codeword* (list-decoding regime nuances are why KPV22 speak of list polynomial commitments); the statement keeps the standard informal claim.

sources.ref_file_title: SW14 - How to Use Indistinguishability Obfuscation Deniable Encryption, and More

pages.class_justification: The construction obfuscates circuits that hardwire the code of the puncturable PRF/PRG derived from the one-way function, so it is non-black-box in the OWF hypothesis (punctured programming is the standard example of a non-black-box use of a primitive; the Asharov-Segev FOCS 2015 framework exists precisely because such constructions fall outside the black-box taxonomy). iO itself is invoked only as an algorithm on circuits. No finer RTV04 placement is stated in the literature, so per the schema convention an explicitly non-black-box construction is recorded as free.
pages.statement: [[indistinguishability-obfuscation|iO]] for all polynomial-size circuits together with a [[hash-function|one-way function]] implies IND-CPA-secure [[public-key-encryption|PKE]]; SW14 also obtain IND-CCA security — [[SW14 - How to Use Indistinguishability Obfuscation Deniable Encryption, and More|SW14]].
pages.sketch: The secret key is a puncturable PRF key $K$; the public key is an obfuscation of the program $(m, r) \mapsto (t, F(K, t) \oplus m)$ where $t = \PRG(r)$. Security: switch $t^*$ to a uniform string outside the PRG's image, puncture $K$ at $t^*$ (the two programs then agree everywhere, so iO hides the switch), and use pseudorandomness at the punctured point.

sources.ref_file_title: GGM86 - How to construct random functions
sources.authors: Oded Goldreich, Shafi Goldwasser, Silvio Micali
sources.note: Sources the PRG => PRF link of the composite chain.

pages.class_justification: Both links are fully black-box: HILL99's PRG construction invokes the OWF only as an oracle and its reduction runs any distinguisher as an oracle, and likewise for the GGM tree (the wiki's black-box-separations page uses GGM as its worked example of the notion). Fully-black-box reductions compose (RTV04).
pages.statement: If [[hash-function|one-way functions]] exist, then [[pseudorandom-function|PRFs]] exist: any one-way function yields a length-doubling [[pseudorandom-generator|PRG]] [[HILL99 - A Pseudorandom Generator from Any One-Way Function|HILL99]], and the GGM tree construction turns the PRG into a PRF [[GGM86 - How to construct random functions|GGM86]].
pages.sketch: GGM defines $\Eval(k, x)$ by walking a binary tree: start from $k$ and, on bit $x_i$, keep the left or right half of the PRG's output; a hybrid over tree levels reduces any PRF distinguisher to a PRG distinguisher. HILL build the length-doubling PRG from any one-way function via hardcore bits and entropy manipulation.
flags: Composite chain OWF => PRG => PRF; both links exist as pages (hash-function-to-prg-hill99, prg-to-prf-ggm86). Repo policy splits composite chains — a human should decide whether to keep this corollary edge.
The composite security loss is dominated by the large polynomial loss of the HILL99 step; not stated crisply enough to fill security_loss.
